papers.title_en: Limited Benefit of Adjuvant Chemotherapy in Pathological Stage II-III Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Lacking Lymphatic, Vascular, and Pleural Invasion.
papers.authors: Hirai Y, Mimae T, Miyata Y, Tsubokawa N, Nagashima T, Kudo Y, Ito H, Ikeda N et al.

papers.ai_note: 非随机回顾性研究，存在明显适应证混杂与治疗选择偏倚（高危且体能状态好者更可能接受AC），摘要未交代倾向评分或对年龄、分期、化疗方案/周期数等的校正细节，高危组OS相差约30个百分点的幅度在观察性数据中可信度存疑。高危组CIR仅相差2.2个百分点却报P = 0.04，与OS巨大差异不相称，数值一致性信息不足。低风险组阴性结论来自亚组分析，摘要未给出该亚组样本量、事件数与检验效能，无法排除假阴性（III类错误）；亦未说明亚组与交互作用检验是否预设，存在多重比较问题。结论中'particularly in pN0'的pN0具体数据摘要未提供，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) improves survival in patients with resected stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, its benefits may not be universal. We aimed to identify subgroups in which the benefit of AC may be limited. METHODS: In this multicenter study, we retrospectively analyzed 1,307 patients with pathological stage II-III NSCLC who underwent complete resection (R0) between 2010 and 2022. Patients were stratified according to the presence of lymphatic (Ly), vascular (V), or pleural (pl) invasion. Overall survival (OS) and cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR) were compared between the AC and non-AC groups using multivariate Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. RESULTS: Overall, 775 patients did not receive AC, and 532 did. In the subgroup without Ly, V, or pl invasion (low-risk group), AC did not significantly improve OS (5-year OS: 79.3% vs. 74.3%, P = 0.66) or CIR (5-year CIR: 28.9% vs. 27.6%, P = 0.79). In patients with Ly, V, or pl invasion (high-risk group), AC was associated with better OS (5-year OS: 81.2% vs. 51.2%, P < 0.01) and lower CIR (5-year CIR: 49.9% vs. 52.1%, P = 0.04). Among patients with pathological node-positive disease (pN+), an OS benefit was observed only in the high-risk group. CONCLUSIONS: In completely resected stage II-III NSCLC, the absence of Ly, V, and pl invasion identified a low-risk subgroup in which the survival benefit of AC appeared limited, particularly in pN0 disease. Pathological invasion status may help identify patients for whom the benefit of AC warrants further evaluation.

papers.authors: Wang S, Zhu J, Jiang J, Feng Y, Ge S, Liang F, Yang X, Zhang Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Surg+HITCH safely improves long-term tumor control in patients with pleural-disseminated TETs. The PTI serves as a practical tool for risk stratification to guide patient selection. Further prospective studies are required to validate our findings.
papers.ai_note: 回顾性研究+PSM固有混杂残留；并发症发生率HITCH组更高（75.0% vs 65.9%），作者以'主要为轻微事件'淡化该差异，且未报告具体并发症分级与统计检验；仅报告PFS未报告OS，3年PFS差异巨大（87.3% vs 48.6%）在回顾性小样本中需警惕；复发率差异未给出统计检验P值；PTI>10阈值缺乏HR/CI/P值支持，验证信息不足
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Our objectives were to evaluate the comparative clinical outcomes of cytoreductive surgery with or without hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITCH) for thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) with pleural dissemination and to assess the utility of a novel Pleural Tumor Index (PTI) as a practical prognostic tool to guide patient selection. METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients with pleural-disseminated TETs who underwent surgery with or without HITCH. The HITCH protocol utilized a standardized sequential dual-agent hyperthermic perfusion (43 °C for 60 mins per session): doxorubicin (25 mg/m2) on postoperative day 1, followed by cisplatin (50 mg/m2) on postoperative day 2. The PTI was used to quantify pleural tumor burden. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline covariates. Perioperative and oncological outcomes were compared. RESULTS: Of 130 enrolled patients, 66 received surgery plus HITCH (Surg+HITCH) and 64 underwent surgery alone, yielding 44 propensity score-matched pairs. Surg+HITCH was associated with improved 3-year progression-free survival (87.3% vs. 48.6%; hazard ratio 0.28; 95% confidence interval 0.11-0.66; P = 0.013) and lower recurrence (9.09% vs. 36.3%). A PTI score >10 indicated a higher risk of tumor progression. Complication rates were slightly higher in the Surg+HITCH group (75.0% vs. 65.9%) but predominantly involved minor events without increasing intensive care unit stay or mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Surg+HITCH safely improves long-term tumor control in patients with pleural-disseminated TETs. The PTI serves as a practical tool for risk stratification to guide patient selection. Further prospective studies are required to validate our findings.

papers.affiliation_highlight: King Edward Medical University, Lahore, Pakistan.

papers.ai_note: 主要终点（插管）获益未转化为任何硬终点（30天/90天/院内死亡率）获益，作者结论已如实说明，但临床解读时须注意插管率可能受通气策略、撤机与插管阈值影响。COVID-19亚组的RR与95%CI [0.65-0.86] 与总体结果完全一致，疑为同一数据集复制或摘要表述重复，信息不足。非COVID亚组点估计更优（0.67）却因CI跨1被判为'不显著'，且交互作用p=0.78提示亚组间无差异，以亚组阴性表述存在误导风险。纳入研究含观察性设计，混杂与插管决策偏倚无法排除。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) are both used to avert invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with pneumonia-related acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), but head-to-head evidence comparing these two modalities specifically, rather than each against conventional oxygen, remains fragmented. METHODS: We searched major databases for studies enrolling adults with pneumonia-related AHRF, including COVID-19-related pneumonia, managed with CPAP versus HFNO. The prespecified primary outcome was intubation within 30 days; secondary outcomes were time to intubation, in-hospital, 30-day, and 90-day mortality, and length of hospital stay. RESULTS: Seven studies (n=1,551), met the inclusion criteria. CPAP was associated with a significantly lower risk of intubation within 30 days than HFNO (RR 0.75 [0.65-0.86], p<0.0001; I2=33%; moderate certainty of evidence). This benefit was significant among patients with COVID-19 pneumonia (RR 0.75 [0.65-0.86], p<0.0001) but not among those with non-COVID-19 pneumonia (RR 0.67 [0.31-1.45]), although no significant subgroup interaction was detected (p=0.78). CPAP was also associated with a significantly longer time to intubation than HFNO (MD 22.27 hours [16.22-28.33]). No significant differences were observed between CPAP and HFNO for 30-day mortality, 90-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, or length of hospital stay. The reduction in intubation was attenuated but persisted when the analysis was restricted to the four randomized trials (RR 0.81 [0.70-0.95]; I2=0%). CONCLUSIONS: In adults with pneumonia-related AHRF, CPAP probably reduces the risk of intubation compared with HFNO without conferring a mortality advantage or reducing length of stay. HFNO remains a reasonable, generally better-tolerated alternative.

papers.ai_note: 主要终点采用研究自定义的'临床获益'，而公认的RECIST 1.1客观缓解仅作为'敏感性终点'，终点层级倒置，存在以非标准终点支撑结论的风险；样本仅76例、无外部验证队列，AUC为发现性结果；PFS分析仅限晚期窗口，系次要/探索性分析而结论将其与主要发现并列表述；结论中'L-window'疑为'late-window'笔误；血清GP73阴性（AUC 0.571、相关P=0.432）在结论中未提及；方向性（GP73升高反而对应获益）与既往组织GP73促癌文献相悖，机制解释信息不足
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Single-time-point tissue-based biomarkers incompletely capture evolving immune states during immunotherapy. This study aimed to dynamically characterize associations linking GP73 levels in peripheral blood T cells and serum to PD‑1/PD-L1 inhibitor response and clinical outcomes in NSCLC patients treated with PD‑1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Intracellular T-cell GP73 was quantified by flow cytometry in available samples from 76 patients from baseline through up to eight cycles. Early sampling was days 1-7; late sampling was day 18 until before the next administration. Mixed-effects models, ROC analyses, and delayed-entry Cox regression assessed dynamics, prespecified study-defined clinical benefit, and progression-free survival (PFS), respectively. Conventional RECIST 1.1 objective response was a sensitivity endpoint. RESULTS: T-cell GP73 declined within cycles (P = 0.012) and rebounded between cycles (P < 0.001). Between-cycle changes differed by clinical benefit status (interaction P < 0.001), unlike within-cycle changes (interaction P = 0.181). T-cell GP73 was higher with clinical benefit (both P < 0.001), with early- and late-window AUCs of 0.865 and 0.772, respectively. RECIST 1.1 sensitivity analyses retained a between-cycle interaction (P = 0.005) and early- and late-window objective-response discrimination (AUCs = 0.761 and 0.808). Serum GP73 showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.571) and no significant correlation with T-cell GP73 (P = 0.432). Higher late-window T-cell GP73 was associated with longer PFS (delayed-entry Cox HR per 100-MFI increase = 0.63, 95 % CI 0.44-0.93; P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: Treatment-cycle-resolved T-cell GP73 monitoring revealed clinical benefit-associated dynamics, while L-window GP73 levels were associated with clinical benefit and progression-free survival in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) is an established first-line therapy for achalasia; however, technical variability persists in key procedural steps. The optimal orientation of mucosal entry remains uncertain. We evaluated whether transverse mucosotomy improves procedural efficiency and reduces gas-related events compared with the conventional longitudinal approach. METHODS: In this multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial conducted at three tertiary centers, 140 adults undergoing POEM were assigned (1:1) to a standardized 15-mm transverse or longitudinal mucosotomy. The primary outcome was time from initial mucosal incision to effective entry into the submucosal tunnel, assessed by independent anonymized video review using predefined objective timestamp criteria. Secondary outcomes included need for hemostasis, mucosotomy closure time, number of clips used, gas-related events, and 30-day complications. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. RESULTS: All randomized patients were included in the primary analysis. Transverse mucosotomy significantly reduced time to submucosal entry (median 228 vs. 269 s; adjusted mean difference - 44 s; 95% CI - 78 to - 10), need for hemostasis (38.6% vs. 57.1%; relative risk 0.68; 95% CI 0.49-0.95), closure time (662 vs. 1020 s; p < 0.001), and number of clips used (median 3 vs. 7; rate ratio 0.44; 95% CI 0.36-0.54). Pneumoperitoneum occurred less frequently with the transverse approach (34.3% vs. 51.4%; relative risk 0.67; 95% CI 0.46-0.97). Rates of serious adverse events and 30-day readmission were low and comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In a multicenter randomized trial, transverse mucosotomy during POEM improved intraoperative efficiency and reduced gas-related events without compromising short-term safety. These findings support mucosal entry orientation as a modifiable technical factor that may optimize procedural workflow and resource utilization in submucosal endoscopic surgery. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRY: NCT07425977.

papers.authors: Martin-Loeches I, Torres A

papers.abstract_en: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a leading cause of hospital and intensive care admission and infectious death in Europe, particularly among older adults, people with multimorbidity, and immunocompromised patients. This Review argues that persistent uncertainty in CAP evidence largely reflects heterogeneity across eight domains: case definition, host, pathogen ascertainment, severity, inflammatory response, treatment exposure, timing and trajectory, and outcome measurement. We examine how these domains distort incidence estimates, pathogen rankings, diagnostic accuracy, severity classification, and trial findings. Within this framework, we highlight developments relevant to Europe: randomised vaccine trials assessing hospitalisation rather than immunogenicity; national data suggesting a changing, increasingly β-lactam-resistant role for Haemophilus influenzae; evidence suggesting that discordant corticosteroid trials reflect heterogeneity of treatment effect rather than drug or protocol differences; and the first randomised trial of host-response-directed immunotherapy in pneumonia-predominant sepsis. We also examine continuing fragmentation in European adult vaccination policy, surveillance, and diagnostic capacity. We propose a diagnostic approach organised by clinical group, a minimum CAP dataset with explicit governance, and a research agenda separating interventions applicable now, evidence required before implementation, and unresolved questions. This approach connects advances in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment with the methodological and organisational changes needed to generate more reliable, clinically actionable European evidence.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Positioning sampling instruments within pulmonary nodules remains a challenge during navigation bronchoscopy. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and needle-based confocal laser endomicroscopy (nCLE) enable tool positioning feedback. However, access to CBCT systems is limited and associated with radiation exposure. To date, no direct comparison between these two modalities has been reported. This study compares CBCT and nCLE for sampling tool position in navigation bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs). METHODS: Twenty-five patients with PPNs scheduled for CBCT-guided navigation bronchoscopy were prospectively enrolled. nCLE imaging, CBCT image acquisition and needle aspiration were performed twice for each nodule, followed by (cryo)biopsies. nCLE videos were evaluated using validated criteria and categorized as tool-in-lesion (TIL) or tool-out-lesion (TOL). CBCT scans were classified as TIL, tool-in-contact (TIC), or TOL. RESULTS: nCLE imaging was performed in 24 patients (nodule was not reached in one), with a median nodule diameter of 19 mm, yielding good-quality images in 22/24 patients (92%). In 77% of these cases, there was an agreement between nCLE and CBCT on the needle position. There were no cases in which CBCT confirmed TIL while nCLE did not. From the five discrepant cases, four were TIC on CBCT, while nCLE was TOL. In one case, there was a complete discrepancy between the techniques with nCLE as TIL and CBCT TOL. CONCLUSION: nCLE and CBCT offer complementary tool position information, with nCLE delivering microscopic-level insights and CBCT providing three-dimensional anatomical context. In environments where CBCT is not available, nCLE may serve as an alternative.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess short-term sex-related differences in subjective outcomes of mandibular advancement device (MAD) treatment among obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients. METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included OSA patients referred for MAD treatment at an academic dental clinic between April 2017 and August 2024. Baseline characteristics included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), and patient-reported OSA-related symptoms. Follow-up evaluations documented OSA-related symptoms, treatment adherence and side effects. Sex-related differences were assessed using Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square test, and repeated logistic regression model. RESULTS: This study included 460 patients (317 [68.9%] males; median [interquartile range] age = 50 [38-59] years, BMI = 26.3 [24.2-29.0] kg/m2, and AHI = 14.9 [9.4-21.4] events/hour). At baseline, females were older, while BMI and AHI did not differ significantly between sexes. Both sexes most frequently reported snoring and daytime fatigue, but females reported more daytime fatigue (P = .05) and breathing pauses during sleep (P = .04) than males. At follow-up, all symptoms decreased (P < .01), without significant sex-related differences. Adherence was similar between sexes, but females more frequently reported difficulty keeping the MAD in the mouth (P < .01) and dry mouth (P = .01). Age-stratified analyses showed no significant differences in baseline symptoms, symptom improvement, adherence, or side effects. CONCLUSION: MAD treatment was associated with reductions in subjective OSA-related symptoms in both sexes, without significant sex-related differences. However, females reported more fatigue and breathing pauses at baseline, and more side effects than males, highlighting sex-related differences in subjective treatment experiences.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Intermittent hypoxemia is increasingly recognized as a stronger predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) than the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). We developed a sound-based AI model to detect oxygen desaturation events and estimate the oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from nocturnal breathing sounds in a fully contactless manner. METHODS: The model was trained using 2,973 nights of synchronized polysomnography (PSG) and audio recordings obtained from hospital- and home-based settings. Validation and independent testing were performed on 664 and 802 nights, respectively. Audio signals were converted into Mel spectrograms and processed using a Vision Transformer-based architecture. Performance was evaluated at the 30-second epoch level using sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, accuracy, and Cohen's κ. ODI estimation was assessed using Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE). RESULTS: For epoch-by-epoch desaturation detection, the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.79, specificity of 0.95, precision of 0.78, F1 score of 0.79, overall accuracy of 0.92, and κ of 0.74. Estimated ODI showed agreement with PSG-derived ODI (r = 0.93, R² = 0.87, p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of -0.29 events/h with 95% limits of agreement from -14.73 to 14.14 events/h. CONCLUSIONS: Breathing sound-based deep learning enables contactless detection of oxygen desaturation events and reliable ODI estimation. This approach may provide a scalable, non-contact method for sleep-disordered breathing assessment in real-world settings.

papers.title_en: Mechanical microenvironment-guided smart nano drug delivery systems for pulmonary fibrosis: from fibrotic delivery barriers to therapeutic remodeling.
papers.authors: Zhou X, Lv Y, Li X, Wang Y, Qin X, Shen S, Zhang Z, Feng Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Pharmacy, Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, Harbin 150040, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Translation of mechanical microenvironment-guided nanomedicine will require clear evidence linking drug delivery to fibrotic lesions, modulation of pathological tissue mechanics, therapeutic efficacy, and long-term safety.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is associated with excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and progressive changes in tissue mechanics, which sustain profibrotic signaling and create additional barriers to effective drug delivery. Fibrotic remodeling alters matrix architecture, interstitial transport, and cellular behavior, while heterogeneous ventilation, airway mucus, and pulmonary clearance further influence the distribution and retention of therapeutic agents. This review examines the mechanical microenvironment in PF and its implications for nanomedicine design. It considers how ECM remodeling, tissue stiffness, and cellular mechanotransduction contribute to disease development and persistence, including their interactions with profibrotic signaling pathways. The effects of structural and mechanical alterations in fibrotic lungs on drug transport and delivery are then examined. Nanomedicine strategies discussed include ECM-targeted and enzyme-assisted approaches to improve tissue penetration, strategies to enhance transport across airway mucus, targeted delivery to mechanically stressed epithelial cells and activated fibroblasts, macrophage-directed interventions, and disruption of pathological crosstalk between mechanical and biochemical signaling. These approaches are assessed in terms of delivery performance, antifibrotic efficacy, and experimental evidence supporting the modulation of cellular or tissue mechanical properties. Emerging mechanically responsive materials are also considered, particularly their potential to exploit mechanical deformation to regulate material function and transport behavior in drug delivery systems. Clinical progress and translational limitations are examined, with emphasis on the evidence needed to advance preclinical strategies toward clinical applications. Translation of mechanical microenvironment-guided nanomedicine will require clear evidence linking drug delivery to fibrotic lesions, modulation of pathological tissue mechanics, therapeutic efficacy, and long-term safety.

papers.title_zh: Five-Year PAP Persistence, Adherence and Patient Follow-up After Implementation of Telemonitoring and Pay-For-Performance in France.
papers.title_en: Five-Year PAP Persistence, Adherence and Patient Follow-up After Implementation of Telemonitoring and Pay-For-Performance in France.
papers.authors: Baillieul S, Alami S, Prigent A, Bianquis C, Diaz Bazin F, Schaller M, Texereau J, Gagnadoux F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Grenoble Alpes University, HP2 Laboratory, INSERM U1300, CHU Grenoble Alpes University Hospital, Grenoble, France.
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Following an important increase in the number of patients treated with positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy in France, a new nationwide model combining telemonitoring and a pay-for-performance scheme was implemented in 2018. OBJECTIVES: To provide a comprehensive overview of 5-year persistence and adherence to PAP therapy and healthcare utilization after the change in the PAP pathway and model. METHODS: This real-world cohort included adults from France started on PAP in 2019-2023. Data sources included provider records (including daily PAP data) and national claims data. Costs were evaluated from the national payer perspective. RESULTS: A total of 84,550 patients (63.7% men, mean age 58.5 years, 53.6% with obesity, mean apnea-hypopnea index 40 events/h) were included; 95.7% used telemonitoring. 58,116 patients had paired claims data. PAP therapy persistence was 83.5% at 1 year, 68.4% at 3 years and 60.5% at 5 years. Main documented reasons for stopping PAP were issues with PAP treatment (54.9%), changes in treatment needs (9.3%) and death (7.0%). There was a dose-effect association between PAP adherence in the first 4 months and 5-year persistence. In the first year of treatment, on average, patients consulted with a general practitioner 6.66 times and with another medical specialist 2.53 times; over the same period home service providers delivered 4.0 interventions at home, 3.6 by phone and 2.8 masks. The number of provider interventions (logistic, educational and supportive) increased as adherence decreased. Mean yearly total cost per patient was €5,462: €1,526 (28%) for hospitalizations, €672 (12%) for disability pensions and sick leave benefits, €436 (8%) for the PAP device, consumables and service, and €415 (8%) for medical consultations. CONCLUSIONS: The proportion of adherent patients at 5 years was high, partly driven by the early discontinuation of patients with low adherence. Alongside intensive medical follow-up, HSPs delivered interventions at greater intensity for patients with low adherence, consistent with the objective of the nationwide telemonitoring and pay-for-performance model. However, solutions are needed for patients who have PAP-related issues and to further reduce the therapy termination rate.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) plus long-acting β2-agonist (LABA) fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) are recommended for symptomatic at-risk patients, and are available on both metered-dose inhaler (MDI) and dry-powder inhaler (DPI) platforms. We evaluated new, locally manufactured MDI and DPI formulations of vilanterol/umeclidinium in Indian adults with COPD. METHODS: Two independent Phase III, randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled non-inferiority trials (MDI study: double-blind; DPI study: open-label) were conducted in India over 12 weeks, using a -100 mL non-inferiority margin for trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). The MDI study (n=226) enrolled adults aged 40-75 years with moderate-to-very-severe COPD, while the DPI study (n=230) enrolled patients with moderate-to-severe COPD. Each trial was analyzed separately, without pooling. RESULTS: Non-inferiority was demonstrated in both studies, with least-squares mean (LS mean) trough FEV1 differences of 49.18 mL (95% confidence interval [CI]: -24.08, 122.43) in the MDI study and 6.1 mL (95% CI: -47.32, 59.46) in the DPI study (Test - Reference; per-protocol population); both lower 95% CI bounds exceeded the -100 mL margin. No statistically significant between-arm differences were detected for secondary endpoints. Adverse events were predominantly mild, with no deaths or serious adverse events over 12 weeks. CONCLUSIONS: Vilanterol/umeclidinium FDC delivered via MDI and DPI was non-inferior to vilanterol/glycopyrronium FDC delivered by the same device type for change in trough FEV1 at 12 weeks in Indian adults with COPD. Longer-term studies in broader populations are needed. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI) CTRI/2025/03/082314 (MDI study) and CTRI/2025/06/088810 (DPI study).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Undernutrition remains a major yet underaddressed determinant of tuberculosis (TB). Although Morocco has made progress in TB control, evidence on the burden and associated factors of undernutrition among patients with TB remain limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the prevalence of undernutrition and severe undernutrition and identify their key factors among adults with TB in Morocco. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among adults with TB attending Tuberculosis and Respiratory Disease Diagnostic Centers (TRDDCs). Nutritional status was assessed using body mass index (BMI). Data were collected on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical presentation, functional status, nutritional and behavioral factors. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were performed to estimate the association between undernutrition and explanatory variables. RESULTS: A total of 431 respondents participated (249 men (57.8%) and 182 women (42.2%), median [IQR] age of 35 [26-52] years). The prevalence of undernutrition among patients with TB was 22.3% (95%CI:18.6-26.5). Severe undernutrition (5.8%) was significantly associated with older age (p=0.030), no formal education (p=0.008), absence of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination (p=0.007) and lack of TB knowledge (p=0.008). In multivariate analysis, the factors associated with undernutrition were: pulmonary TB (AOR=1.90, 95%CI [1.07-3.38]), smoking (AOR=2.21, 95%CI [1.05-4.63]) and having less than three meals per day (AOR=3.24, 95%CI [1.74-6.04]). In our study, family size over four was a protective factor from undernutrition (AOR=0.53, 95%CI [0.30-0.92]). CONCLUSIONS: Undernutrition among patients with TB in Morocco is multifactorial. This underscores the importance of targeted advocacy for nutritional interventions and strengthened support for patients with TB in Morocco.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: In non-invasive home mechanical ventilation (NIV) using single-limb circuits with vented masks, supplemental oxygen can be added at different locations, potentially resulting in variable delivered inspired oxygen fractions (FiO₂). Recommendations and data comparing oxygen inlet positions are lacking. METHODS: A lung simulator study was conducted using a 1.8 m single-limb NIV circuit with a vented mask. Oxygen was added at three locations: the ventilator oxygen port, a bleed-in connector near the ventilator outlet, and a bleed-in connector between the tube and mask. Oxygen flow rates of 1, 2, and 3 L/min were tested. Three simulated conditions were studied by adjusting lung compliance and airway resistance: healthy, COPD, and obesity. NIV was applied in pressure-controlled ventilation mode. Settings were EPAP/IPAP 4/14 cmH₂O for the healthy model, and both 4/18 and 8/20 cmH₂O for the COPD and obesity models, with a respiratory rate of 14/min. Mean resulting FiO₂ and minute ventilation from three repeated measurements in random order were recorded. RESULTS: Oxygen delivery via the ventilator oxygen-port and ventilator-near bleed-in produced broadly similar FiO2 values, ad both generally higher FiO₂ than mask-near delivery. Differences between inlet positions became more pronounced at higher oxygen flows reaching a maximum absolute difference of 5.3 percentage points between oxygen port an mask-near delivery. FiO₂ also differed between the two tested ventilator pressure settings in the COPD and obesity simulations, despite only small differences in minute ventilation. Increasing oxygen flow increased FiO₂ across all configurations, although the magnitude of this effect depended on oxygen-injection location and the simulated condition. CONCLUSION: In this lung simulator study using a single-limb NIV circuit with a vented mask, oxygen injection location influenced the achieved FiO₂. Under the tested conditions, oxygen delivery via the ventilator oxygen port and a ventilator-near bleed-in connector resulted in broadly similar FiO₂ values and generally achieved higher FiO₂ than mask-near delivery. These findings warrant validation across different ventilators, circuits, interfaces, and pressure settings.

papers.title_en: Escape at an immunodominant SARS-CoV-2 spike epitope is not compensated by variant-specific CD8 T cells in HLA-A⁎24:02+ individuals.
papers.authors: Li H, Aritsu Y, Nakama T, Wall A, Jin Y, Goto Y, Tajima Y, Yamada K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Human Molecular Immunology, Joint Research Center for Human Retrovirus Infection, Kumamoto University, Kumam…

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告任何样本量、效应量、检出率、CI 或 P 值，核心结论（NF9-5R 特异性 T 细胞 not detected）为定性判断，缺少检测下限与统计学支撑。标题与结论表述为体内无补偿，但研究同时鉴定出可同时识别两种肽及表达 L452R 细胞的交叉反应 TCR（12E），且该反应仅在体外 priming 后才可检出，提示'无补偿'部分依赖检测方法敏感性，体内是否完全缺失证据不充分；结论由体外体系与小鼠模型外推至人群疫苗策略。
papers.abstract_en: The antiviral CD8 T cell response is critical for controlling viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2. Spike mutations can mediate escape from pre-existing T cell immunity but it remains unclear whether such variants induce variant-specific CD8 T cells. Here, we investigate the HLA-A⁎24:02-restricted immunodominant NF9/A24 epitope (S448-456) and its prevalent L452R variant (NF9-5R) in Omicron BA.5 convalescents. NF9-5R-specific CD8 T cells are not detected ex vivo or after short-term in vitro stimulation of PBMCs, despite robust responses to other epitopes. In HLA-A24 transgenic mice, NF9 is markedly more immunogenic than NF9-5R, with rare cross-reactive responses. However, in vitro priming of NF9-5R-reactive CD8 T cells enables identification of a cross-reactive TCR (12E) recognizing both peptides and cells expressing spike L452R. Although the NF9-5R peptide can thus be presented and recognized, escape at an immunodominant epitope is not compensated by variant-specific CD8 T cells in vivo, creating functional "blind spots" relevant to vaccine strategies.

papers.title_zh: Emerging molecular probes for lung cancer: Targets, translational evidence, and theranostic potential.
papers.title_en: Emerging molecular probes for lung cancer: Targets, translational evidence, and theranostic potential.
papers.authors: Yu Z, Sun X, Wang P, Zheng M, Xing L, Sun X
papers.affiliation_highlight: Center for Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging, Shandong Cancer Hospital and Institute, Shandong First Medical Univer…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality worldwide, and the management of both non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has entered the era of precision medicine. METHODS: This review summarizes current progress in radiolabeled molecular probes for lung cancer. Radiotracers were categorized according to their molecular targets, with emphasis on design strategies, preclinical and clinical evidence, current limitations, and potential theranostic applications. RESULTS: Evidence ranged from preclinical studies to validated diagnostic or predictive performance, with occasional management changes. EGFR and FAPI imaging supported mutation assessment, response prediction, and staging, while immune-targeted probes characterized checkpoint heterogeneity and immune-cell distribution. MET, HER2, folate receptor alpha, and CXCR4 imaging showed early human feasibility; ALK and CTLA-4 imaging remained predominantly preclinical. Choline and FLT imaging assessed metabolism and early pharmacodynamic responses. Theranostic strategies enabled target confirmation and dosimetry, with FAPI-directed therapy entering clinical investigation and CXCR4-, CD133-, and DLL3-directed therapies showing preclinical efficacy. Translation still requires standardized thresholds, prospective validation, and evidence of benefit from imaging-guided decisions. CONCLUSIONS: Molecular probes should be advanced according to the clinical decision they are intended to inform, not target expression alone. Prospective trials must compare imaging-guided pathways with FDG PET/CT and tissue-based standards and must measure downstream treatment selection and patient-important outcomes before routine implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy has emerged as a crucial component in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Nevertheless, interindividual variability in efficacy, along with both primary and acquired resistance, as well as immune-related adverse events, continue to limit the benefits for patients. The gut microbiota and its associated metabolites are believed to play a significant role in pulmonary immune regulation via the gut-lung axis, with alterations in this system being associated with NSCLC development and progression, as well as the outcomes of immunotherapy. This review summarizes the key features of gut microbial and metabolic profiles in patients with NSCLC, focusing particularly on the mechanisms by which short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, gut microbiota-associated Trp metabolites, and other microbial metabolites may influence the tumor immune microenvironment and responses to immunotherapy. Furthermore, we consider their potential value in supporting NSCLC diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and treatment-response prediction. Therapies aimed at targeting metabolic pathways, fecal microbiota transplantation, dietary interventions, and microbiome-based preparations present additional avenues for enhancing the efficacy of NSCLC immunotherapy and managing treatment-related toxicity. However, current evidence primarily stems from small clinical studies and animal models, while methodological discrepancies and limited causal evidence impede clinical translation. Future research that integrates longitudinal multi-omics analyses, metabolic tracing, and controlled clinical trials is essential to elucidate the clinical significance of the gut microbiota-metabolite axis in NSCLC immunotherapy and precision medicine.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced lung injury (SLI) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Endothelial cell (EC) ferroptosis contributes to SLI, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of CDKN1A in pulmonary EC ferroptosis during SLI. METHODS: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were performed to identify ferroptosis-related endothelial targets and signaling pathways. CDKN1A expression and PI3K/AKT signaling were validated in cecal ligation and puncture-induced SLI mice and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated primary murine pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (MPVECs). Functional studies were conducted using the CDKN1A inhibitor UC2288, CDKN1A siRNA, a PI3K inhibitor, and a PI3K agonist. RESULTS: Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified CDKN1A as a key ferroptosis-related endothelial gene associated with PI3K/AKT signaling. CDKN1A expression and PI3K/AKT activation were increased in SLI lung tissues and LPS-treated MPVECs. CDKN1A inhibition or silencing attenuated ferroptosis, as evidenced by reduced PTGS2 and TFRC expression, restoration of SLC7A11 and GPX4, decreased ferroptosis-associated fluorescence, and alleviation of mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. PI3K inhibition phenocopied the protective effects of CDKN1A knockdown, whereas PI3K reactivation reversed these effects in CDKN1A-silenced MPVECs. CONCLUSIONS: CDKN1A promotes pulmonary EC ferroptosis in SLI, at least in part, through activation of PI3K/AKT signaling. Targeting the CDKN1A-PI3K/AKT axis may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for SLI.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder impairing mucociliary clearance. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of clinical and genetic characteristics in a large Turkish cohort with frequent parental consanguinity. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed on 145 patients (selected from 361) with regular follow-up since 2017 to ensure longitudinal data consistency. The diagnostic work-up included nasal nitric oxide measurement and high-speed videomicroscopy, while confirmation was established through genetic testing and/or transmission electron microscopy. Patients were classified according to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework. Patients were evaluated for clinical predictors, longitudinal pulmonary function, and genotype-phenotype correlations based on structural protein localization. RESULTS: Among 145 patients (mean age 15.91 ± 6.26 years), early diagnosis was significantly associated with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (p = 0.014), NICU admission (p < 0.001), situs inversus totalis (p < 0.001), and congenital heart disease (p < 0.001). The mean PICADAR score was 7.8 ± 3.4, showing a moderate negative correlation with age at diagnosis (r = -0.50, p < 0.001). According to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework, 63 patients (43.4%) were classified as confirmed PCD, 13 (9.0%) as PCD highly likely, and 69 (47.6%) as suspected PCD. Among confirmed PCD patients, the most frequent genetic findings were DNAH5, CCDC40, and DNAAF1. Lower final FEV1 values were observed in selected rare genotype subgroups, particularly CCNO, although variant-specific comparisons were limited by small subgroup sizes. CONCLUSION: Early recognition of neonatal respiratory distress requiring NICU admission and laterality defects, particularly situs inversus totalis, remains critical for reducing diagnostic delay. In populations with high consanguinity, genetic testing is particularly important for confirming diagnosis and identifying potentially high-risk genotypes. Multidisciplinary follow-up focusing on nutrition, infection control, and preservation of lung function is essential for long-term care in PCD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly prevalent and aggressive malignancy often characterized by lymph node metastasis, a key contributor to its poor prognosis. Although NSUN2 functions as an oncogene in LUAD through m5C-dependent mechanisms, its specific role in regulating malignant progression remains elusive. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of NSUN2 in regulating this progress. METHODS: Cell viability and proliferation of A549 and PC9 cells were detect by cell-counting kit-8 and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) staining. Migration and invasion were evaluated by Transwell and wound-healing assays. Flow cytometry was performed to detect apoptosis, whereas Western blot was performed to evaluate the levels of proteins related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and lymphangiogenesis (Snail, vimentin, MMP2, MMP9, vascular endothelial growth factor C [VEGF-C] and E-cadherin). A LUAD xenograft model was constructed using BALB/c nude mice. The underlying mechanism was investigated by methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP), RIP, RNA pull-down, and the like. RESULTS: NSUN2 expression was upregulated in LUAD tumor tissues and cell lines. In nude mice, NSUN2 knockdown inhibited A549 and PC9 cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, as well as xenograft tumor growth and VEGF-C expression. Mechanically, NSUN2 knockdown reduced Notch1 mRNA stability by decreasing its m5C modification. Overexpression of Notch1 reversed these inhibitory effects both in vitro and in vivo. CONCLUSION: Collectively, the study demonstrated that NSUN2 promoted LUAD progression through m5C-dependent Notch1 stability. These findings highlight the NSUN2-Notch1 m5C-dependent regulatory axis as a promising target for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION AND AIM: Multidrug- and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in the WHO European Region. This critical narrative review examines how social determinants influence the clinical course and outcome of patients across the MDR/RR-TB care cascade, from access to diagnosis and treatment initiation to treatment support, retention in care. METHODOLOGY/SCOPE: Researchers reviewed the current publications on the topic of our review until June 2026. Sources were prioritized on the basis of relevance to MDR/RR-TB, social determinants, and care-cascade outcomes. Evidence from broader TB populations was used only when MDR/RR-TB-specific data were limited and is identified as such. MAIN FINDINGS: Across settings, poverty, catastrophic total costs, homelessness, incarceration, stigma, education, mental-health difficulties, substance use, and barriers related to legal status, mobility, language, insurance, and access to care were associated with delayed diagnosis. Material, psychosocial, and individualized treatment support may improve retention and outcomes, but much of the evidence is observational and context-specific. CONCLUSION: Social determinants should be addressed throughout the MDR/RR-TB care cascade through patient-centered models that combine effective regimens with financial, psychosocial, housing, and individualized adherence support. The evidence base remains heterogeneous, and causal claims should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is marked by alveolar epithelial injury, and promoting alveolar regeneration is a promising therapeutic strategy. Maresin1 (MaR1), a specialized pro-resolving mediator, exhibits anti-inflammatory and pro-regenerative properties; however, its role in alveolar epithelial regeneration remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether MaR1 alleviates lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute lung injury (ALI) by promoting alveolar epithelial regeneration and to elucidate the involvement of the Rac1-WASF2-Arp2/3 pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An LPS-induced ALI mouse model was established, and primary alveolar type II (AT2) cells were isolated from rats. Lung injury was assessed by histopathology (H&E) and immunofluorescence for AT2 (pro-SFTPC), intermediate transition cells(Krt-8) and AT1 (PDPN) markers. AT2 cell proliferation and transdifferentiation were evaluated by flow cytometry (cell cycle analysis), qRT-PCR (SPC and AQP5), and alveolar organoid formation assays. Pharmacological inhibitors CK666 (Arp2/3 complex inhibitor) and NSC23766 (Rac1 inhibitor) were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Protein-level validation was performed by GTP-Rac1 pull-down and Western blotting. RESULTS: MaR1 treatment significantly reduced pulmonary inflammation (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α) and promoted recovery of alveolar structure. MaR1 enhanced AT2 cell proliferation (increased KI67+cells and G1-to-S/G2 phase transition), reduced transitional Krt8+intermediate cells, and increased AT1 cell marker expression (PDPN, AQP5). MaR1 also improved alveolar organoid formation, size, and the proportion of PDPN+ organoids. Notably, CK666 and NSC23766 abolished MaR1-mediated AT2 proliferation, transdifferentiation, and alveolar structural repair. Mechanistically, MaR1 activated GTP-Rac1 without altering Rac1 gene expression, and upregulated WASF2 and Arp3 at both mRNA and protein levels, whereas Arp2 remained unchanged, indicating that MaR1 promotes alveolar regeneration via the Rac1-WASF2-Arp2/3 pathway. CONCLUSION: Maresin 1 promotes alveolar epithelial regeneration in LPS-induced acute lung injury via the Rac1-WASF2-Arp2/3 pathway. These findings highlight epithelial regeneration as a critical determinant of recovery in ARDS and suggest that MaR1 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for acute lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: Respiratory tract infections continue to represent a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality. Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) are highlighted as key etiologic agents of bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in children under two years old. Recurrent infections during the second year of life may be associated with significant histopathological damage and might also be a risk factor for developing chronic pulmonary diseases, such as non-atopic asthma. In adults, these viruses similarly elevate clinical burden on the elderly and individuals with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), causing the exacerbation of respiratory signals and symptoms and, consequently, promoting a chronic inflammatory response that modifies the lung tissue and disease progression. Tissue repair and the homeostasis recovery might be associated with the participation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs), both lung resident and migratory MSCs, these cells are characterized by their plasticity and immunomodulatory capacity, which are relevant to restoring tissue homeostasis after injury. However, RSV and HMPV may also infect MSCs, raising the question that infected MSCs could lose immunomodulatory efficacy and plasticity, thereby affecting tissue renewal. This review aims to provide an overview of the effect of respiratory viral infections, their implications in the lung tissue damage and the possible participation of MSCs in the recovery of lung homeostasis by tissue repair and immune response modulation.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous pulmonary disorder characterized by persistent respiratory symptoms and significant extrapulmonary complications. Skeletal muscle dysfunction, a prominent comorbidity, severely compromises exercise capacity and quality of life and independently predicts mortality. While pharmacological therapies effectively control respiratory symptoms, they have limited efficacy against COPD-associated muscle atrophy and functional decline, and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. The RANK/RANKL signaling pathway, a key mediator of muscle-bone crosstalk, is markedly upregulated in COPD and contributes to its musculoskeletal pathology. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the RANK/RANKL pathway in COPD, with a dedicated focus on its mechanistic role in driving skeletal muscle pathology. We emphasize the pathway's role in driving proteolysis via the NF-κB/ubiquitin-proteasome system, impairing myogenic regeneration, sustaining chronic low-grade inflammation, and dysregulating metabolic and calcium homeostasis. These multifaceted pathological effects enable the RANK/RANKL pathway to bridge pulmonary inflammatory injury to peripheral skeletal muscle wasting, thereby representing a plausible therapeutic target to mitigate COPD-related systemic myopathy beyond conventional pulmonary-directed treatments.
